---
title: "Reference"
---

## Command line

`python -m src.lowpoly_pdf_to_svg [options]`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `data/example/example.yaml` | Project YAML manifest |
| `--output` | the YAML's folder, `data/<project>/` | Output directory |
| `--dpi` | `180` | PDF render resolution |
| `--page` | all pages | Convert only this 1-based page; repeatable |
| `--pdftoppm` | `pdftoppm` | Poppler `pdftoppm` executable |
| `--allow-no-ocr` | off | trace even without Tesseract; edge numbers become `?` and glues no longer pair (by default a retrace without Tesseract stops with an error) |

## Make targets

| Target | What it does |
|---|---|
| `make` | Convert every page in the manifest into `data/<project>/<project>.svg` |
| `make page PAGE=4` | Convert one page into `output/<project>/page-4/` |
| `make export` | Last step: `data/<project>/<project>-export.svg` with short glue-pair labels and cardstock fills, see [Export SVG contract](export-contract.qmd) |
| `make assembly` | Build order from the folded model: `data/<project>/assembly.json` and `assembly.csv`, see [Build order](usage.qmd#build-order) |
| `make export-check` | Rebuild the synthetic export fixture and check it against the contract |
| `make install` | Install the Python dependencies |
| `make report` | Render this site into `report/_site` |
| `make preview` | Serve this site on localhost and re-render on save |
| `make report-data` | Write the summary statistics the public site is built from into `report/data/<project>/` |
| `make clean` | Remove generated output |

## Manifest

```{.yaml filename="data/example/example.yaml"}
project: example

source:
  pdf: example.pdf         # in data/, not committed
  page_size: letter
  credit: "Template designer (year)"   # optional: printed on the head-fit drawings

folds:                     # which printed line style is which fold
  dash_dot: mountain       # Pepakura default; swap if a template
  dashed: valley           # draws mountain folds dashed

output:
  default_sheet: a4        # a4 or 12x12 for nesting

materials:                 # one entry per cardstock colour
  - id: red
    name: Red cardstock
    pages: [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]
  - id: brown
    name: Brown cardstock
    pieces: [piece-04-06, piece-05-06]   # cut from brown although page 4 and 5 are red

tabs:                      # optional: glue tabs generated at export (default on)
  depth_mm: 7.5            # tab depth from its fold: half a 15 mm tape (the PDF's are about 5.6 mm)
  flap_mm: 15              # flap tongue width, one full tape width; 0 for none
  flap_length_mm: 18       # how far the tongue reaches from the fold (15-20 mm)
  flap_area_mm2: 5000      # seams between two pieces this big get a flap on their longest glue
  flap_edge_mm: 25         # ... when that glue is at least this long
  stress_top: 0.1          # share of seams with the most load in fold3d.json that get a flap; 0 for none
  flaps: [piece-07-03, 412]  # stress points (piece ids or PDF numbers), twins follow
  extra_flaps: [piece-24-*]  # these pieces' plain glue edges get a flap too; twins follow
  generate: true           # false: keep the traced tabs, add only the extra flaps
  angle_deg: 45            # slope of the tab ends
  margin_mm: 0.8           # clearance from the partner face's folds and cuts
  gap_mm: 1                # clearance between two tabs of one piece
  keep: [green]            # materials already cut: keep their traced tabs
# tabs: false              # keep the PDF's traced tabs everywhere

export:                    # optional
  numbers: build           # piece numbers in build order (make assembly); pages: page order, for pieces already cut

reference:                 # optional: the finished model, checked by the 3D fold
  parts: 1                 # glues into one piece
  openings: 4              # holes left open (e.g. two eyes, mouth, neck)
  symmetric: true          # every piece has a mirror twin
  triangles: 1238          # face and corner counts, when the finished model is known
  corners: 633
```

A page belongs to one material (`pages:`). A page whose pieces are cut from more than one
cardstock lists the odd pieces under their own material (`pieces:`, the trace's piece ids); a
material may have only `pieces:`. Such a piece carries its own `data-material` and sits in its
cardstock's layer, so the export colour, the glue units and the 3D colours follow it. Moving a piece
needs no retrace: `make redo` with no pages rebuilds the SVG from the saved traces.

`make -f fold3d.mk` compares each `reference:` count it knows (`triangles`, `corners`, `parts`,
`openings`) with the folded trace in `fold3d-baseline.csv`. A part is a set of pieces held together
by closing glues. An opening is one closed run of rim, where an edge belongs to one surface face
only. Glue tabs are not surface.

With `symmetric: true`, the fold also holds mirror twins to each other. Twins come from the trace's
`mirror-mismatches.csv`, and their surface corners are matched on the flat pattern, mirrored. Pairs
whose corners do not mirror within 1 mm stay untied; their tabs are never tied. After the settle pass,
each tied corner is pulled onto the mirror image of its twin's corner across the plane the twins agree
on best, and the plane is fitted again between rounds. A pair far from mirrored pulls less, so a pair
traced differently cannot pull the glue apart. `fold3d-baseline.csv` adds `mirrored_pairs`: tied pairs
that fold to within 2 mm of mirrored, against all tied pairs.

## Outputs

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `data/<project>/<project>.svg` | One Inkscape SVG, one row of pages per cardstock (not committed); document size in inches, drawing in millimetres |
| `data/<project>/previews/page-PP-<material>.png` | Each PDF page as rendered for tracing (not committed) |
| `data/<project>/fold3d-mirror.csv` | Each tied twin pair: how well its flat corners mirror (`flat_rms_mm`), how far the folded pair is from mirrored (`folded_mm`) and `mirrors` (within 2 mm) or `differs`, worst first |
| `data/<project>/mirror-fixes.csv` | What the mirror-twin step changed: corners moved (`move`), folds added (`add`), fold styles matched (`style`), each with its reason |
| `data/<project>/edge-numbers.csv` | One row per printed edge number, read by the [glue pairs](glue-pairs.qmd) page |
| `data/<project>/README.md` | Conversion status and edge check; its first paragraph is shown on the home page |

### Edge table columns

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `number` | The printed edge number, as text (leading zeros kept) |
| `piece` | Piece id `piece-PP-NN`, PP the PDF page |
| `side` | `edge`, `tab` or `none` (no cut edge found under the number) |
| `length_mm` | Length of that edge |
| `x_mm`, `y_mm` | Position of the number on its page |
| `ocr_trusted` | `yes` when the number was read with confidence |
| `partner_piece`, `partner_side`, `partner_length_mm` | The other place the same number is printed |
| `length_diff_mm` | Difference between the two edge lengths |
| `status` | `ok`, `length mismatch`, `both tabs`, `no tab`, `unpaired`, `line not found`, `printed N times` |

## Head fit {#head-fit}

`make -f fold3d.mk headfit` (or `python -m src.lowpoly_pdf_to_svg.headfit --config …`) puts a
real head shape inside the folded model (`fold3d.json`): the MakeHuman base mesh (CC0) from the
neck up, `assets/head/makehuman-head.obj`, scaled to the head's circumference above the brows
(`scripts/make-head-mesh.py` rebuilds it from MakeHuman). By default the wearer looks out through
the model's eye openings (the largest mirrored pair in front), so the mask is turned to face where
they face; for Bowser the snout then hangs down to the chest. The head stands upright and, from
chin to crown, must be completely inside the card (the neck and shoulders may pass the rim): the fit is the smallest scale, from the eye scale (pupil distance /
opening spacing) up, at which the head keeps `clearance_mm` of air with the card at most 5 mm into
the shoulders. The mask rests as low as it can, on the crown or on the shoulders, whichever it
meets first (`rests_on` in `head-fit.json`). The pupils may then sit below the eye openings; a ray
straight ahead from each pupil finds where to cut a sight hole. `rule: eyes` restores the older fit,
which centres the openings over the pupils and only reports the head room (on Bowser the crown then
comes through the top). With `eyes: free` the mask faces the `front` axis and is scaled until the
head just fits. `look_up_deg` is how far the wearer must look up to see out of the eye openings (to their lower edge, to their centre). `eye_offset_mm` gives how far the pupils sit behind and above (+) or below (-) the eye openings. `height_cm` scales the shoulders and chest by body height against the preset's reference height (Swedish 18-year-olds, 180.4/167.6 cm; child: 8-year-olds, 130.5 cm; Albertsson Wikland et al. 2002), while the head keeps its own size. Bowser: female 86 % (crown meets the hair; pupils 40 mm behind, 35 mm below the openings), male 91 %, child 83 %. A run takes 10 to 15 minutes and does not change the
pattern. Scaling the export itself is the next step (issue #79); until then, resize every sheet by
the same percentage in Cricut Design Space.

The 3D viewer shows the fitted head inside the mask when `head-fit-mesh.json` is next to
`fold3d.json`; the **head** switch hides it.

```yaml
fit:
  head: female            # child | female | male
  circumference_mm: 545   # optional: tape round the head above brow and ears; scales the preset
  eye_distance_mm: 61     # optional: pupil to pupil
  scale: 1.0              # optional: hang the mask at this size instead of finding the smallest
  height_cm: 175          # optional: body height; sizes the shoulders and chest (default: Swedish mean for the preset)
  eyes: openings          # openings (default) or free
  rule: inside            # inside (default: whole head inside) or eyes (openings over the pupils)
  clearance_mm: 0         # air between head and card (default 0: it rests on the head)
  sight_hole_mm: 30       # sight hole diameter with eyes: free (default 30)
  up: +y                  # roughly up, in the folded model's axes
  front: eyes             # the way the eye openings face, or an axis such as -y
```

The presets are rounded means (adult men and women in the style of ANSUR II, and a child of about
eight); a measured circumference and pupil distance are better. One head shape is scaled for all
of them; the pupil distance only moves the pupil marks.

| Make variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `HEAD=child` | Fit this preset instead of the YAML's |
| `COMPARE=1` | Also print the fit of every preset |

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `head-fit.json` | Head used, `scale`, `eyes`, `eye_scale_range` (scales that keep each pupil 5 mm inside its opening), mask size at that scale, pupil position, `tip_deg`, `tightest_mm` (head room), and per eye: `through` (`card` or `opening`), the `piece`, distance ahead and the hole centre on the flat piece (`flat_mm`, pattern millimetres before scaling) |
| `head-fit-mesh.json` | The fitted head and shoulders in the folded model's axes, for the 3D viewer |
| `head-fit-views.svg` | A4: front and side of the scaled mask with the head and lines of sight |
| `head-fit-eyes.svg` | A4 at 1:1 (print at 100 %): the eye openings at the fitted scale with the pupils, to hold to the face; with `eyes: free`, each piece the eyes look through with the sight hole to cut |

## 3D fold-up

`make -f fold3d.mk` (or `python -m src.lowpoly_pdf_to_svg.fold3d --config …`) folds the traced
pieces into `data/<project>/fold3d.obj` and its tables. A cold build of a large model takes about
half an hour, so later runs reuse earlier work. On Bowser (4 cores), a warm run that moves
every unit takes about 4.5 minutes, and a run after a one-unit edit takes about 5 seconds.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--gape` | `3.0` | Let go of a glue whose ends stay this far apart (mm) |
| `--anneal` | `5` | Cycles of hard then easy fold pull after the build |
| `--cold` | off | Ignore saved poses and caches and place every piece from scratch (`COLD=1` in Make) |
| `--rejoin` | off | Let the join move every unit, not only the units changed since the saved pose (`REJOIN=1` in Make) |

Mirror twins (pieces whose faces mirror each other) are pulled towards mirrored poses while the
glue settles. Twins still far from mirrored after that are snapped: the side with more open glues
is laid exactly onto the mirror image of the other, worst pair first, and the glue settles again
(`mirror snap` in the log). A flap whose sides match a tab on its twin is marked as a tab too, so twins keep the same surface
(the traced shape is not changed).

### Modular glue plan

The glue is planned in three stages, and `fold3d.py` folds in the same order:

1. **By cardstock.** Pieces are split by their material.
2. **Glue units.** Within one cardstock, pieces tied by a numbered glue (a tab onto a face)
   form one glue unit. A piece with no glue to another piece of its colour is a unit of its own.
   Each unit is folded on its own.
3. **Joins.** The glues between units of different cardstocks close last, by moving whole units.

`make -f fold3d.mk plan` writes the plan in a few seconds from `<project>.svg`, without folding;
when a `fold3d-glue.csv` from an earlier fold is there, its statuses fill the `closes` columns.
A full fold writes the same files.

| File | One row per | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `fold3d-units.csv` | glue unit | `unit` (`<cardstock>-NN`, largest first), `material`, `pieces`, `glues` inside the unit, `closes`, `piece_ids` |
| `fold3d-joins.csv` | pair of units with glues between them | `unit_a`, `unit_b`, `materials`, `glues`, `closes`, `numbers` (PDF numbers) |

`fold3d-glue.csv` has a `stage` column: `unit` for a glue inside one unit, `join` for one between
units. Next steps, folding only changed units and joining on
demand, are tracked in issue #37.

### Warm start and component cache

- **Same-cardstock components.** The glue units of the plan above, each folded on its own as a
  subassembly. Glues between cardstocks are then
  closed by moving whole components, with local refinement around the joins. A join that cannot
  close stays open and is reported in `fold3d-glue.csv`. It is never forced.
- **`fold3d-components.json`** caches each component's pose. Its key covers the component's
  traced geometry, tab marks and internal glues, so an edit only rebuilds the components it
  touches.
- **`fold3d-state.npz`** is a pose checkpoint for the whole model. The first warm run falls back
  to the previous `fold3d.json`. Vertices are matched by piece id and flat position, rounded to
  0.01 mm. When at least 70 % match, their 3D positions are reused, and new or moved vertices are
  placed by aligning their piece to its unchanged corners. The piece-by-piece placement is then
  skipped.
- **Only changed units move in the join.** The checkpoint also records the glues between units.
  On a warm run, the join moves only the units that were rebuilt, plus the units whose glues to
  other units changed. Every other unit keeps its saved pose. With nothing changed, the join
  does no work. `--rejoin` moves every unit again, and so does a first run from `fold3d.json`,
  which has no join record.
- **The join solve is sparse.** Each join glue ties only two units, so finite differences are
  grouped by unit and the solve reads only the corners at the joins. The fold-pull cycles stop
  early once a cycle changes neither the wrong-fold count nor the closed-glue count.
- Log lines start with the elapsed time (`[mm:ss]`).
- A missing, unreadable or poorly matching cache falls back to a cold build. Both caches are
  written only after a successful run, and Git ignores them.
- **`fold3d-tab-overrides.json`** (optional, hand-kept) maps a face `piece-PP-NN/k` to `true`
  (glue tab) or `false` (body) where the automatic tab marking got it wrong. The viewer keeps
  the same overrides while you edit.
